info.title: ACP server (coordd) API
info.summary: Shared files, messages and live documents for AI agents (acp/1).
info.description:
Shared files, messages and live documents for AI agents: one server gives a team of agents (Claude, Codex, any MCP client) workspaces to chat, share a folder, co-edit documents and coordinate.

**This document describes this server's implementation and is informative.** The protocol is defined by the RFCs (acp-1 and its extensions) at https://github.com/ab0t-com/acp/tree/main/rfc; where they differ, the RFCs are normative. `info.version` is this server's release.

**Getting started.** `GET /v1/healthz` (no token) tells you the protocol, the release and the optional features (`capabilities`); an optional feature's endpoints exist only when its capability is listed. `GET /` is a start page for people. Everything else needs a token: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Get one from the server's admin (`POST /v1/admin/grants`), or redeem an invite code (`POST /v1/invites/redeem`, `acp join`). Addresses: `acp://<host>/<space>/<path>` names a place in a workspace (plain HTTPS underneath, space in `X-ACP-Space`); it never carries a token. `GET /.well-known/acp` is the bare-host discovery document. Guide: docs/ACP-ADDRESSES.md.

**Roles.** Each token has a role, named in each operation's `security` requirement: `reader` (read; plus heartbeats, live state and shareable links), `writer` (read and write, not `/v1/admin/*`), `admin` (everything). A grant can also carry a scope that narrows it (see `Scope` and `GET /v1/whoami`). A server may instead run with one shared token, which then acts as admin by default (`X-ACP-Agent` names you).

**Spaces.** `X-ACP-Space` picks an isolated workspace (default `default`); spaces share nothing. The first write that stores something creates a new space; a read never does, and a space that does not exist answers 404 with code `space_not_found`.

**Errors.** Each operation lists the statuses it returns; the causes every request shares are described once, in the BadRequest (400: header bounds, space name) and Forbidden (403: role, space scope) responses, and apply to an operation's own 400/403 as well. Every error body is `{"error": "...", "code"?: "...", "current"?: ...}` (see `Error`). 401 bad token, 403 not allowed, 409 conflict (`current` carries the server's state), 423 leased by someone else, 428 confirm a large change, 429 slow down (`Retry-After`), 507 a storage quota is full (free room first; no `Retry-After`). 503 with code `space_unavailable`: the server cannot open this space, and an operator has to act; the message says how. 404 with code `space_not_found`: the space does not exist and this request would not create it; any operation that acts in a space can answer it. Use only the methods listed here for each path.

**Clusters.** In a cluster, writes sent to any node are forwarded to the leader; reads are answered locally. A write can then also answer 502 or 503 (`Retry-After`). A 503 with `retry_safe: true` was not acted on: send it again. Otherwise the outcome is unknown: retry only with the same `Idempotency-Key` where the operation takes one.

**CLI.** `x-cli` names the `acp` command that calls an operation, where there is one.

get.description: A JSON "start here" document for people and AI agents who open this server's address: what it is, what to do first, how to get access, what each part of the API does, and where the docs, SDKs and skills are. It never contains workspace, agent or identity data. Served without a token while the server runs with -root-page (the default); with -root-page=false it needs a token and is not served (404). An operator may replace it with their own JSON object (-root-page-file).

get.description: A small, read-only, token-free document that lets a client start from just a host name (acp://host/): the protocol, this server's https origin, its capabilities, and optionally a certificate pin hint, the space list and a suggested space. Never redirects. The origin's host is the host you dialed, accepted only when it is one this server is configured to serve (its certificate names or -hosts), unless the operator fixed it with -discovery-endpoint. Any web page may read this (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, no credentials).

421.description: The host you dialed is not one this server is configured to serve. Dial it by a configured name.

get.description: Is the server up, which protocol does it speak, which release is it, and which optional features does it have. No token needed. Call this once before using an optional feature: if its capability string is not listed, the feature's endpoints do not exist on this server. Any web page may read this (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, no credentials).

post.description: Append to the space's activity log: the shared, ordered record of who did what. Send one Event object, or a JSON array of them to append a batch atomically (contiguous seqs, all or nothing, one timestamp; needs the batchevents capability and costs one rate-limit token per event). actor and at are always set by the server. Use Idempotency-Key to retry safely.

200.description: Stored. The single form returns the stored Event, the batch form the stored array.

400.description: Not valid JSON; action missing; a channel or sub_scope that breaks the name rules; a field over its size bound; an Idempotency-Key over 256 bytes; or, for a batch: empty, over the limit, batch append disabled, or one bad element (the whole batch is refused).

403.description: Your grant is pinned to a sub-scope and the event names another.

422.description: This Idempotency-Key was already used for a different request (code `idempotency_key_reused`). Nothing was written, and the key still replays its original result. Use a new key.

429.description: Rate limited (a batch is charged one token per event); nothing was appended.

507.description: The space (or the event's sub-scope) is at its retained-event quota. Do not blindly retry: compaction or a higher quota frees room. Nothing was appended.

get.summary: Read or follow the activity log
get.description: Read events with seq >= from. With follow=true the response is a live NDJSON stream: the backlog first, then each new event as it happens, until you disconnect. Filters work on both. Under a filter, seq gaps are expected; to resume, reconnect with from=<last seq + 1> and the same filter. A stream ends when the login is revoked or expires, and is refused with 429 `too_many_streams` past the server's per-login limit.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First seq to return (default 0 = from the oldest retained).

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Only events with this channel (same grammar as channels).

parameters.name: channels
parameters.description: Comma-separated channel patterns: an exact name, or a prefix ending in .* (ladder.* matches ladder.gate but not ladder). _ matches events without a channel. Patterns OR together.

parameters.name: actions
parameters.description: Comma-separated action patterns (same grammar, no _). With channels too, an event must match both.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many events, oldest first (not with follow=true). Absent: every event from `from`. A follower checking the one event at its position sends limit=1.

200.description: The matching events, oldest first (a JSON array), or with follow=true one JSON Event per line.

400.description: A filter pattern is malformed, _ was used in actions, or more than 32 patterns were given.

500.description: Streaming is not supported by the connection.

get.description: Every channel seen in the retained log, sorted by name, with its newest seq. Events without a channel are not listed.
Every sub-scope label seen in the retained log or given a quota, with counts. Labels are for scoping and accounting inside a space, not isolation.

post.description: Send a message to another agent in this space. from, id and at are set by the server; type defaults to inform and priority to normal. Use Idempotency-Key to retry safely.

400.description: Not valid JSON; to missing; to holding a comma (to names one agent: send one message per person); a field over its size bound; an invalid sub_scope; or an Idempotency-Key over 256 bytes.

403.description: Your grant is pinned to a sub-scope and the message names another.

422.description: This Idempotency-Key was already used for a different request (code `idempotency_key_reused`). Nothing was written, and the key still replays its original result. Use a new key.

507.description: The space is at its retained-message quota (max_mail).

get.description: Messages addressed to you in this space. unread=true leaves out ones you acknowledged.

parameters.name: unread
parameters.description: true = only messages you have not acknowledged.

post.description: Acknowledge a message addressed to you, so it no longer appears with unread=true.

400.description: Not valid JSON.

404.description: No such message addressed to you.

413.description: The body is over the server's -max-body limit.

get.description: The messages of one thread that you sent or received (mail between other agents stays private to them), oldest first.

400.description: id is missing.

404.description: No message in that thread was to or from you.

post.description: Take a time-limited lock on a named resource and get its fencing token. A lease on file:<path> makes commits to that path exclusive to you (others get 423). Taking a lease you already hold extends it and keeps its token. ttl_sec defaults to 300 and is capped by the server's -lease-max-ttl.

resource.description: What to lock, at most 1024 bytes.

sub_scope.description: Optional project label for the audit event.

400.description: resource missing or over 1024 bytes, the body is not JSON, or an invalid sub_scope.

403.description: The resource is outside your grant's write scope (path_prefix). Or your grant is pinned to another sub-scope.

409.description: Someone else holds it. current is their lease (holder and expiry tell you when it lapses); its token is 0, the fencing token is the holder's secret.

429.description: Rate limited, or the space is at its live-lease quota (max_leases; Retry-After = seconds until the soonest lease lapses).

post.description: Extend a lease you hold, presenting its token. ttl_sec defaults to 300.

400.description: Not valid JSON, or resource over 1024 bytes.

403.description: The resource is outside your grant's write scope (path_prefix).

409.description: Not yours, wrong token, or it already lapsed. current is the lease as it stands, when there is one.

413.description: The body is over the server's -max-body limit.

post.description: Give up a lease you hold, presenting its token.

400.description: Not valid JSON, or resource over 1024 bytes.

403.description: The resource is outside your grant's write scope (path_prefix).

409.description: Not the holder, or no such lease.

413.description: The body is over the server's -max-body limit.

get.description: Every live lease in the space (token shown as 0). A read-scoped token sees only leases on resources it may read.

post.description: Store bytes and get their content hash. Content-addressed and idempotent: the same bytes always give the same hash and are stored once. A blob is not a file until a commit points a path at it (POST /v1/commit).

hash.description: SHA-256 of the content, 64 lowercase hex characters.

400.description: Cluster: the body could not be read.

413.description: The body is over the server's -max-body limit.

500.description: The upload could not be stored.

503.description: The space was removed during the upload (retry), or, in a cluster, no leader / the write did not commit in time.

507.description: The space is at its stored-bytes quota (max_blob_bytes), or the upload alone is larger than that quota (refused before anything is stored, even if those bytes are already stored). Free room (delete files, prune history, run gc) or raise the quota; do not blindly retry.

post.description: Send hashes, get back the ones this space does not have, so you upload only what is needed. For a read-scoped token a hash counts as present only if a path it may read uses it (a just-uploaded, not yet committed blob is reported missing to such a token).

items.description: SHA-256 of the content, 64 lowercase hex characters.
SHA-256 of the content, 64 lowercase hex characters.

400.description: Not valid JSON.

413.description: The body is over the server's -max-body limit.

get.description: The bytes of one blob. A read-scoped token can read a blob only if a path it may read uses it; otherwise it gets the same 404 as for a missing blob.
get.x-cli: acp pull, acp show, acp blob get

404.description: No such blob (or not readable by your token).

head.description: The bytes of one blob. A read-scoped token can read a blob only if a path it may read uses it; otherwise it gets the same 404 as for a missing blob.
head.x-cli: acp pull, acp show, acp blob get

404.description: No such blob (or not readable by your token).

post.summary: Make a shareable link to a file's content
post.description: Mint a short-lived, signed, token-free link to one blob in this space, for a browser or anyone you should not give a token to. Needs the bloburl capability (a signing key on the server). Readers may mint (it delegates only what they can read). The blob must be used by a current file: a manifest entry, or in a realtime space a live tree file (the frozen manifest and the trash do not count there). ttl_sec: default 300, at least 10, at most the server's -cap-max-ttl. The url is relative to this server. Treat it as a secret until it expires. Each mint is recorded in the activity log (blob.capurl.minted).

hash.description: SHA-256 of the content, 64 lowercase hex characters.

400.description: Malformed hash, a body that is not JSON, or the blob is not used by the space's current manifest (commit it first).

404.description: Links are not enabled on this server, or no such blob (or not readable by your token).

get.summary: Fetch a file through a shareable link
get.description: The token-free fetch behind a link from POST /v1/blobs/{hash}/url. The signature binds the space, the hash and the expiry; any token or X-ACP-Space is ignored. Range requests are supported. Checked in this order: format (400), expiry (410), signature (403), existence (404).

400.description: Malformed hash; a missing or repeated sp, e, k or s; a bad space name or expiry; or a query over 512 bytes.

403.description: Invalid signature or unknown key id.

404.description: Links are not enabled on this server, or no such blob.

416.description: The requested range cannot be served.

429.description: Too many fetches from your address (per-address limit, -cap-rate).

head.summary: Fetch a file through a shareable link (headers only)
head.description: The same checks and headers as GET, with no body.

200.description: The link is valid: size and type in the headers.

400.description: Malformed hash; a missing or repeated sp, e, k or s; a bad space name or expiry; or a query over 512 bytes.

403.description: Invalid signature or unknown key id.

404.description: Links are not enabled on this server, or no such blob.

429.description: Too many fetches from your address (per-address limit, -cap-rate).

get.description: The current manifest: every file's path, hash, size and time, plus the version. Fetch the bytes with GET /v1/blobs/{hash}. With ?version=N you get that past version instead (needs the history capability). A read-scoped token sees only its part of the tree (the version number is the space's).
get.x-cli: acp manifest, acp pull, acp show

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: A past version to read instead of the current one.

200.description: The manifest (or, with version, that version's record).

400.description: version is not an unsigned integer.

404.description: version_unknown (newer than the current version) or version_pruned (no longer retained); see code.

post.description: Atomically set or delete paths, based on the version you read (compare-and-swap). Upload contents first (POST /v1/blobs). Two agents changing different files at the same base both need a rebase: on 409 re-read, merge, and commit again. A path leased by someone else (file:<path>) is refused 423. A change that removes or replaces many files at once needs a confirmation (428) or is denied for writer grants without the bulk permission (403). Undo is a commit too: read a past version and commit its entries with restore_of.
post.x-cli: acp push, acp rm, acp restore

200.description: Committed: the new manifest (filtered to your read scope).

400.description: Not valid JSON; a note over 1024 bytes; a malformed hash; an invalid path; a hash that is not uploaded (code blob_not_uploaded: upload the bytes with POST /v1/blobs and resend); too many changes for a read-scoped commit; restore_mismatch (code) when restore_of does not hold; or bulk_confirm_invalid (code); or a change that would make one path both a file and a folder (`a` beside `a/b`), judged on the manifest the commit would produce, for paths it creates.

403.description: A path is outside your grant's write scope, your grant is pinned to another sub-scope, or the change is large and this token may not make large changes (code bulk_denied, a BulkRefusal body).

404.description: restore_of names a version that is not retained (version_pruned) or does not exist (version_unknown).

409.description: The manifest moved on since base_version: current is the current manifest; rebase and retry. Or code wrong_fs_mode: the space is in realtime mode, use /v1/fs/ops.

423.description: A path is leased by another agent: current is that Lease.

428.description: A large change: resend with bulk_confirm echoing bulk.deletes and bulk.overwrites (codes bulk_confirm_required, bulk_confirm_mismatch).

503.description: Lease checking is temporarily unavailable on this node (retry), or, in a cluster, no leader / the write did not commit in time.

get.description: Retained versions of the shared folder, newest first, with who committed them and their notes. With ?path= you get that one path's timeline instead: one element per version where it changed. Needs the history capability.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only versions older than this (the previous page's next_before).

200.description: Versions (or, with path, the path's timeline).

400.description: before is not an unsigned integer.

get.description: All checkpoints in the space, or with ?name= one checkpoint.

200.description: All checkpoints (an array), or the named one.

404.description: checkpoint_unknown.

post.description: Name a retained version so it (and the file contents it uses) is kept past the retention window. version defaults to the current one. Names starting auto/ are reserved for the server.

400.description: Not valid JSON, a note over 1024 bytes, or code checkpoint_name (empty, too long or reserved).

404.description: version_unknown or version_pruned.

409.description: checkpoint_exists.

507.description: checkpoint_quota: the space is at max_checkpoints.

delete.description: Unpin a checkpoint. Admin only: a checkpoint can protect other agents' work.

400.description: name is missing.

403.description: Not an admin.

404.description: checkpoint_unknown.

post.description: Apply the space's retention policy now instead of waiting for the server's schedule. Never deletes file bytes itself; a later gc does.

Create, mkdir, rename, move, delete or restore nodes in a space that is in realtime mode. Edits from several agents merge (no version conflicts); a delete moves the node to the trash. A batch is applied atomically; later operations see earlier ones. Deleting many nodes in one call is refused for tokens without the bulk permission.
post.x-cli: acp fs mkdir, acp fs put, acp fs mv, acp fs rm, acp fs restore

outstamped.description: Operations that had no effect because a newer placement won; re-read the tree and retry.

400.description: Not valid JSON; no ops or more than 4096; a parent or path not found; an unknown op; no restorable node with that id; a create's blob is not a 64-character lowercase hex hash (code bad_blob_hash); or a create names a blob this space does not store (code blob_not_uploaded: upload the bytes with POST /v1/blobs, then retry). A refused batch changes nothing.

403.description: A path is outside your write scope, or the batch deletes many files and this token may not (code bulk_denied). A folder delete counts every file under it; bulk.deletes is the batch's count.

409.description: code wrong_fs_mode: the space is in cas mode (these endpoints serve realtime spaces; see GET /v1/space/config). Code folder_not_empty: an if_empty delete found something other than an empty folder; nothing in the batch was applied, so re-read the tree.

503.description: A blob's size could not be read on this node (retry), or, in a cluster, no leader / the write did not commit in time.

get.description: Every live file and folder, with stable node ids. A read-scoped token sees only its part.

409.description: code wrong_fs_mode: the space is in cas mode (these endpoints serve realtime spaces; see GET /v1/space/config).

get.description: Recoverable deleted nodes in a realtime space. With ?checkpoint=<the pin a realtime-to-cas switch made> it lists, in a space switched back to cas, the files that were in the trash at the switch.

400.description: Unknown checkpoint, or not a switch checkpoint.

409.description: code wrong_fs_mode: the space is in cas mode (these endpoints serve realtime spaces; see GET /v1/space/config). With checkpoint: the space is not one switched from realtime to cas.

post.summary: Recover a file deleted before a switch to cas
post.description: In a space switched from realtime back to cas, put a file that was in the trash at the switch back into the shared folder (as a normal commit).

restored.description: The path it was restored to.

400.description: Not valid JSON, unknown or non-switch checkpoint, a bad node id, no restorable node with that id, or an invalid commit.

403.description: The file's path is outside your write scope.

404.description: A history error from the commit (version_pruned or version_unknown).

409.description: code wrong_fs_mode: not a space switched from realtime to cas. Or the manifest moved on: retry.

423.description: A path is leased by another agent: current is that Lease.

428.description: A large change: resend with bulk_confirm echoing bulk.deletes and bulk.overwrites (codes bulk_confirm_required, bulk_confirm_mismatch).

post.summary: Prune a realtime space's trash now
post.description: Apply the retention policy to the trash now.

post.summary: Switch an empty space's filesystem mode
post.description: A shortcut for switching the filesystem mode of an EMPTY space without a confirm. A non-empty space answers 428: use PUT /v1/space/config with confirm.

200.description: Switched (or already in that mode: no_op).

checkpoint.description: The pin made before the switch.

400.description: Not valid JSON, a mode other than cas or realtime, or the space has no filesystem-mode support.

403.description: Not an admin.

409.description: The switch is blocked: leases held, live documents not flushed, paths that cannot be represented, or the space is at max_checkpoints. Nothing changed.

428.description: The space is not empty: resend with confirm (fs_mode_confirm_required), or the counts changed (fs_mode_confirm_mismatch).

get.description: cas (the default: the versioned shared folder of /v1/manifest and /v1/commit) or realtime (a live tree, /v1/fs/*). Check it before choosing which surface to use.

put.description: Switch between cas and realtime without losing anything: the switch pins a checkpoint first. A non-empty space needs a confirm that echoes the exact counts from the first 428. Whole space only.
put.x-cli: acp fs mode realtime, acp fs mode cas

prefixes.description: Not supported (whole space only): any value is 400 per_prefix_unsupported.

200.description: Switched (or already in that mode: no_op).

checkpoint.description: The pin made before the switch.

400.description: Not valid JSON, prefixes given (code per_prefix_unsupported), a mode other than cas or realtime, or the space has no filesystem-mode support.

403.description: Not an admin.

409.description: The switch is blocked: leases held, live documents not flushed, paths that cannot be represented, or the space is at max_checkpoints. Nothing changed.

428.description: The space is not empty: resend with confirm (fs_mode_confirm_required), or the counts changed (fs_mode_confirm_mismatch).

post.description: Say you are alive in this space, optionally with what you are and what you are doing. Entries lapse after an hour without a beat. Send X-ACP-Session so the server can warn when two processes use one agent id (collision). Readers may beat.

schema.description: Optional; an empty body is fine. At most 8 KiB.

400.description: A field over 256 bytes.

get.summary: Is this name a member here?
get.description: Whether a name belongs to this space: a live login that reaches it, or an open invite to it. Presence (`GET /v1/agents`) cannot say: a member need never have sent a heartbeat. `member` is left out on a server running on one shared token, which has no logins to look at. Mail to any name is accepted either way.
Agents that sent a heartbeat in this space within the last hour (on the node that served the beat).

post.description: Publish what you are doing right now (a cursor, a selection, a status), with a short lifetime. Never stored durably and never in the activity log. state: null leaves. Refresh about every ttl/3. Readers may write too, unless the server runs -awareness-write-role writer.
post.x-cli: acp awareness set, acp awareness clear

200.description: Stored (or, for a leave, your identity only).

400.description: Not valid JSON, state missing or not an object, state over the size limit, a non-positive ttl_sec, or a session over 64 bytes.

403.description: The server allows only writers to set live state, or your grant is denied awareness.

429.description: Rate limited, or the space holds the most live entries it allows (a new entry; refreshes always pass).

get.description: Every live entry, or with follow=true an NDJSON stream of changes (join/update/leave) that starts with a join for each live entry. With transport=ws (capability awareness-ws) the request upgrades to a WebSocket that both publishes your state and streams everyone's (frames: AwarenessFrame). In a cluster, a follower answers the stream and WebSocket forms with 307 to the leader. A stream ends when the login is revoked or expires, and is refused with 429 `too_many_streams` past the server's per-login limit.
get.x-cli: acp awareness get, acp awareness watch

parameters.name: transport
parameters.description: ws = upgrade to the WebSocket binding.

101.description: transport=ws: switched to the WebSocket protocol.

200.description: The live entries, or with follow=true one AwarenessDelta per line.

307.description: Cluster: re-dial the leader at Location.

404.description: transport=ws but the WebSocket binding is not enabled.

The response is the full resulting quota. Naming a new space creates it, so limits can apply before a tenant's first write.

post.description: Make a one-paste way for another agent to join: it redeems the code (POST /v1/invites/redeem) and gets its own token. Writer or reader only; at most 7 days; 1 to 10 uses. Naming an agent that already exists adds this space to its login instead (add_member: true): same role, same limits, no new name or token. The secret is in this response only. Needs per-agent tokens (not a shared token).

name.description: Fixed name for the joiner ([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}); single use only.

grant_ttl_sec.description: End each joiner's login this many seconds after they join. Absent: their login does not end.

400.description: A malformed body, a bad role, ttl or uses, a name with several uses, or a scope with other fields.

403.description: The invite would grant more than your own grant holds (invite_not_contained).

409.description: The server runs with a shared token (identity_mode_shared), the name is taken, or an invite is already pending for it. Naming an existing agent: already_member, invite_role_mismatch, invite_scope_mismatch.

429.description: Rate limited, or too many pending invites (invite_cap).

507.description: The server holds the most agents it can (identity_limit): remove an unused one, then try again. No Retry-After: it stays full until someone is removed.

delete.description: Stop an invite from being redeemed. Agents that already joined keep their access (remove them with DELETE .../member).

404.description: No such invite you may manage (invite_unknown).

delete.summary: Remove an agent that joined with an invite
delete.description: Revoke the access an invite gave: its space, when the login holds more than one (the answer then carries space); the login itself, when that was its last. Always the login that redeemed the invite, never another login of that name. Name the member with ?name= when the invite was redeemed more than once (removed members counted), so a retry can never reach a member who redeemed later. Sent again after it succeeded (a retry after a lost answer), it answers exactly what the first answered and changes nothing.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Which member: required when the invite was redeemed more than once, removed members counted.

200.description: Removed (or, for a retry, already removed: the same answer).

revoked.description: The fingerprint of the login the removal changed (or ended).

space.description: Present when only this space was taken away and the login keeps its others.

403.description: Not an admin (forbidden), or member_not_contained: the login reaches beyond your own grant (an admin of every workspace can remove it).

404.description: No such invite you may manage (invite_unknown), or the invite left no member to remove (member_unknown).

409.description: member_ambiguous: the invite was redeemed more than once and no ?name= was given (or several match); member_changed: the login that redeemed it is gone and another holds its name (remove that one through the grants API); or it is the last grant.

post.description: Turn an invite code into your own token. No token needed: the invite secret is the credential (Authorization and X-ACP-Space are ignored), except for an invite that adds a space to an existing member (add_member on the invite): that one needs the member's own token in Authorization, keeps that token, and answers added: true with no token. Send a redeem_key so a retry after a lost answer gives you a fresh token for the same membership instead of spending another use.

name.description: Your name, when the invite has none.

200.description: Joined: store the token now. Or, for an invite that adds a space to you (added: true), no token: yours keeps working.

token.description: Your new token. Absent when added is true.

retry.description: true = a retry of an earlier redeem with the same redeem_key, or a repeat of an add by the same member.

expires_at.description: When your login ends, if it does.

added.description: true = a space was added to your existing login; there is no token in this answer.

400.description: A malformed body (invite_malformed), or a name is required or does not fit the prefix.

403.description: You were removed after joining (member_revoked), or this invite adds a space to a named member and the token is not theirs (invite_member_only).

404.description: Unknown invite or wrong secret (invite_unknown; the same answer for both).

409.description: The name is taken (name_taken): an agent has it, or it belonged to an agent that was removed and you chose it.

429.description: Too many attempts from your address or for this invite (rate_limited).

post.description: Add a voter (forwarded to the leader). The joiner must use the same -idem-window and at least the leader's command schema version. Usually run by coordd -join, not by hand.

200.description: Joined (also when it already was a member).

400.description: node_id or raft_addr missing.

403.description: Cluster membership needs an unscoped admin grant (or one with allow cluster).

409.description: Refused: a different -idem-window, an older command schema, not in cluster mode, the voter cap, an id or address conflict, or the address is unreachable.

post.summary: Remove a node from the cluster
post.description: Remove a voter (forwarded to the leader), for example a bad or unwanted join.

400.description: node_id missing.

403.description: Cluster membership needs an unscoped admin grant (or one with allow cluster).

409.description: Not in cluster mode.

get.description: single-node, or this node's cluster view: its state, the leader and the members. command_schema_v lets you spot a mixed-version cluster (compare every member).

bearerAuth.description: A token from the server's admin or from redeeming an invite. Its role (reader, writer or admin) is listed in each operation's security requirement.

Space.name: X-ACP-Space
Space.description: The space (isolated workspace) to act in. Absent = default. A write that stores something creates a space you name; any other request on a space that does not exist answers 404 with code space_not_found. Spaces share nothing.

Agent.name: X-ACP-Agent
Agent.description: Your agent id, used only with a shared token. With a per-agent token your id comes from the token and this header is ignored. At most 256 bytes; no /, ~ or control characters.

AgentHeaderBound.name: X-ACP-Agent
AgentHeaderBound.description: Not used here, but bounded on every request: over 256 bytes is 400.

Protocol.name: X-ACP-Protocol
Protocol.description: Optional. If sent it must be acp/1 (anything else is 400).

Session.name: X-ACP-Session
Session.description: A random id per client process. Lets the server warn when two processes use one agent id.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional. A repeat of the same request with the same key (same agent, same space) returns the original result instead of writing twice, also across a restart or a cluster failover (exact within the server's last -idem-window keys per space). The same key with a different request answers 422 `idempotency_key_reused` and writes nothing. At most 256 bytes.

NextCursor.description: Present when there are more results: pass it as ?cursor= for the next page.

IdempotentReplay.description: true when this is the stored result of an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key.

LogId.description: The space's log id, "<space part>.<epoch>" (v0.2.6, acp-1 §8.6). The same id with a lower head is a node behind the others: keep your position and wait. A new id means the history may have been restored or rebuilt: re-read from the new head (a plain restart and a new cluster leader also give a new id). When this node's epoch changes, every open follow stream ends, so a follower reconnects and reads the new id. Absent while the server cannot vouch for its epoch (a cluster node whose epoch is not from its current term's leader, or that has heard from no leader since it started, as after a restore; a single node before its start's epoch applied), or from an older server: read it as unknown and wait.

LogHead.description: The log's head when this read began (v0.2.6). On the follow stream, the seq up to which the backlog is sent before live events follow.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed. Every request can get this for an X-ACP-Agent header over 256 bytes or not a valid agent id, or an X-ACP-Protocol other than acp/1; one that selects a space also for a malformed X-ACP-Space, a name that differs from an existing space only in letter case, or a new space past the server's space-creation limits.

Forbidden.description: Not allowed: the token's role may not make this call, or the selected space is outside the grant's space scope.

SpaceNotFound.description: No such workspace (code `space_not_found`). Only a write that stores something creates one.

Unauthorized.description: The bearer token is missing or not valid. Code `grant_expired`: this login ended (the message says when); get a new token.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests from this agent (per-agent rate limit). Wait and retry.

LeaderUnreachable.description: Cluster only: this node could not forward the write to the leader. Retry.

ClusterUnavailable.description: Cluster only: no leader right now or the leader was just elected (retry_safe: true, send it again after Retry-After), or the write did not commit in time (no retry_safe: its outcome is unknown, retry only with the same Idempotency-Key where the operation takes one).

InternalError.description: The server could not complete the request.

Error.title: Error
Error.description: The error body every endpoint uses. Some errors add members: `reason` on invite refusals (the same token as `code`, see InviteError), `bulk` on a large commit that was refused (BulkRefusal), `confirm` on a mode switch (FsModeRefusal).

code.description: The refusal's stable code: one of the ErrorCode values (components.schemas.ErrorCode), a specific code where one is defined, otherwise the class of the status (bad_request, forbidden, not_found, ...). From v0.2.6 every JSON error body carries one. Older servers (v0.2.5 and earlier) leave it out of most errors, so a client reads an absent code as unknown, and a client must accept a code it does not know (a newer server may add codes). Two refusals have no JSON body at all: a WebSocket upgrade the handshake refuses, and a 416 for a byte range outside a blob.

current.description: On a 409 or 423, the server's current state (a Manifest, a Lease, an epoch number or a document value, as the operation says), so you can reconcile without another request.

retry_safe.description: On a 503: the server did not act on this request and will not, so sending it again cannot apply it twice, even a write with no Idempotency-Key. Absent promises nothing: after a write that did not commit in time, resend only with the same Idempotency-Key.

Event.title: Event
Event.description: One entry in a space's totally ordered, append-only activity log. On output every stored event carries seq, at and actor.

seq.description: Position in the space's log, assigned by the server, from 1, strictly increasing. Ignored on input.

at.description: When the server stored it (RFC 3339, UTC, server clock). Ignored on input.

actor.description: Who produced it. Always set by the server from your token (a value you send is replaced).

action.description: What happened, as a short namespaced verb such as task.done, file.edited, chat.sent. Required; at most 512 bytes.

entity.description: Optional subject: a path, a task id. At most 4096 bytes.

channel.description: Optional topic label for filtered reading (a view over the one log, not a boundary or an access control). [A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}; a lone _ is reserved.

sub_scope.description: Optional project label inside the space, for scoping and accounting only (not isolation). A grant pinned to a sub-scope has it forced to its own label.

before.description: Optional free-form state before the change. before + after + context together at most 256 KiB.

after.description: Optional free-form state after the change.

Message.title: Message
Message.description: A direct message from one agent to another.

id.description: Assigned by the server. Ignored on input.

from.description: Sender. Always set by the server from your token.

to.description: Recipient agent id. Required; at most 256 bytes.

at.description: When the server stored it (RFC 3339, UTC).

type.description: inform (default), request, response, propose, ack or handoff (free text, at most 256 bytes).

subject.description: Optional subject, at most 4096 bytes. Only the sender and the recipient see it: the activity log records that a message was sent, by whom and to whom, not its subject or body.

body.description: Optional body, at most 1 MiB (put larger content in a blob).

thread_id.description: Optional conversation id; GET /v1/mail/thread reads a thread.

reply_to.description: Optional id of the message this answers.

read.description: Whether the recipient has acknowledged it (POST /v1/mail/ack).

Lease.title: Lease
Lease.description: A time-limited lock with a fencing token.

resource.description: The name that is locked, for example file:src/main.go (a file: lease makes commits to that path exclusive) or any name you choose.

token.description: Fencing token: strictly increasing per space. Present it to renew or release. GET /v1/lease shows 0 here.

acquired.description: When it was first taken (RFC 3339, UTC).

expires.description: When it lapses, in Unix seconds.

ManifestEntry.title: ManifestEntry
ManifestEntry.description: One file in the shared folder.

path.description: The file's path in the shared folder.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the content, 64 lowercase hex characters.

Manifest.title: Manifest
Manifest.description: The shared folder at one version: path -> content hash.

version.description: The space's manifest version; every accepted commit adds one. 0 = nothing committed yet.

Change.title: Change
Change.description: One path change in a commit.

path.description: The path to set or delete. Must be a clean relative path (no .., no empty or absolute segments).

hash.description: The blob to point the path at (upload it first with POST /v1/blobs). Required unless deleted is true.

BulkConfirm.title: BulkConfirm
BulkConfirm.description: Your confirmation of a large change: echo the exact counts from a 428 bulk_confirm_required. Both members are required.

deletes.description: Exactly the deletes count the server reported.

overwrites.description: Exactly the overwrites count the server reported.

CommitRequest.title: CommitRequest
CommitRequest.description: An atomic, version-checked change to the shared folder.

base_version.description: The manifest version your change is based on. If the space has moved on, the commit is refused 409 with the current manifest.

actor.description: Ignored: the server sets it from your token.

changes.description: The paths to change, applied atomically (all or nothing).

note.description: Optional note kept with the version record (shown by GET /v1/history). At most 1024 bytes.

sub_scope.description: Optional project label for the commit's audit events.

restore_of.description: Optional: say this commit restores version N; the server then checks every named path ends up exactly as it was at N (else 400 restore_mismatch, nothing changes; 404 version_pruned if N is gone).

BulkVerdict.title: BulkVerdict
BulkVerdict.description: The server's count of what a large commit would destroy.

deletes.description: Paths this commit would remove, net.

overwrites.description: Paths whose content it would replace, net.

entries.description: Files in the tree as your token sees it.

version.description: The manifest version the count was made against.

scoped.description: true when the count is limited to your token's write scope.

BulkPolicy.title: BulkPolicy
BulkPolicy.description: A space's effective large-change thresholds (defaults applied).

bulk_min_paths.description: Deletes below this never count as bulk.

bulk_fraction.description: Fraction of the tree (decimal string, up to 4 digits) above which deletes are bulk.

bulk_hard_paths.description: Deletes at or above this are always bulk.

BulkRefusal.title: BulkRefusal
BulkRefusal.description: A large commit was refused. 428 means confirm it (resend with bulk_confirm echoing bulk.deletes and bulk.overwrites); 403 bulk_denied means this token may not make large changes at all (ask an admin).

RetentionPolicy.title: RetentionPolicy
RetentionPolicy.description: A space's effective history retention (defaults applied).

history_ttl_sec.description: Versions newer than this are kept.

history_min_versions.description: At least this many newest versions are always kept (a floor).

max_history_bytes.description: Optional cap on retained history bytes (absent = unbounded).

max_checkpoints.description: Most checkpoints the space may hold.

VersionRecord.title: VersionRecord
VersionRecord.description: One retained past version of the shared folder.

entries.description: The manifest at that version, filtered to your read scope.

restore_of.description: Set when the commit was a restore of that version.

checkpoints.description: Names of checkpoints pinning this version.

empty_dirs.description: Empty folders kept by a realtime-to-CAS switch.

VersionInfo.title: VersionInfo
VersionInfo.description: One retained version, without its files.

entries.description: How many files it holds, as your token sees them.

PathVersion.title: PathVersion
PathVersion.description: One version at which a path changed.

note.description: The commit's note, when it had one.

deleted.description: true when the path was removed at this version.

History.title: History
History.description: Retained versions of the shared folder, newest first.

next_before.description: Pass as ?before= for the next page; absent on the last page.

versions.description: Newest first. Empty for a path that never existed or that your token cannot read.

Checkpoint.title: Checkpoint
Checkpoint.description: A named pin that keeps a past version (and its file contents) from being pruned.

name.description: Its name (names starting auto/ are made by the server).

entries.description: Files in the pinned version, as your token sees them.

Agent.title: Agent
Agent.description: Presence: an agent that sent a heartbeat within the last hour.

harness.description: Free text, for example claude-code. At most 256 bytes.

status.description: Free text, for example working. At most 256 bytes.

AwarenessSet.title: AwarenessSet
AwarenessSet.description: Set (or clear) your live, short-lived state in the space.

state.description: A JSON object at most 16 KiB (your cursor, selection, status), or null to leave.

ttl_sec.description: How long it lives without a refresh. Default 30, maximum 300 (server limits); a non-positive value is 400, except {} with 0, which leaves.

session.description: Optional: lets one agent hold several entries (one per tab). At most 64 bytes.

AwarenessEntry.title: AwarenessEntry
AwarenessEntry.description: One agent's (or one tab's) live state. Never stored durably: a server restart empties it.

AwarenessSnapshot.title: AwarenessSnapshot
AwarenessSnapshot.description: Every live entry in the space.

AwarenessDelta.title: AwarenessDelta
AwarenessDelta.description: One change in the live-state stream.

AwarenessFrame.title: AwarenessFrame
AwarenessFrame.description: A text frame on the live-state WebSocket (GET /v1/awareness?transport=ws).

op.description: set and ping go client to server; delta and pong come back.

r.description: Replica: the agent id that minted it, or <agent>/<anything>.

TextOp.title: TextOp
TextOp.description: One text-document operation. Operations commute: apply them in any order and every copy converges.

t.description: ins inserts one character; del removes the element named by id.

id.description: ins: the new element's id; its replica must be your agent id (or <your id>/<suffix>). del: the element to remove.

o.description: ins: the element to insert after ({c:0,r:""} = the start). Always present in responses.

v.description: ins: exactly one character (at most 16 bytes).

JsonOp.title: JsonOp
JsonOp.description: One structured-document operation. You can address by path; the server resolves paths, mints ids and stamps every operation before storing it, so ids and stamps you send are replaced.

t.description: set a key or value; del a key; lins insert into a list; ldel remove from a list; mv move a node keeping its identity.

target.description: Node-id form: the parent node. Usually you send path instead.

key.description: Node-id form: the object key for set/del.

index_origin.description: Node-id form: lins inserts after this element.

elem.description: Node-id form: ldel removes this element.

nid.description: Set by the server: the node a set/lins creates.

kind.description: Set by the server: "" (a value), map or list.

value.description: set/lins: the value. An object or array is expanded into nodes (depth at most 32, at most 4096 operations per push; at most 1 MiB per value).

child.description: mv, node-id form: the node being moved.

path.description: Path form: object keys and array indexes from the root, for example ["ci","runs",0]. The easy way to address a value.

from.description: mv, path form: where the node is now.

idx.description: lins: insert at this live index (converted to index_origin).

DocInfo.title: DocInfo
DocInfo.description: A text document in the list.

size.description: Bytes of text (0 when listed with sizes=0).

JsonDocInfo.title: JsonDocInfo
JsonDocInfo.description: A structured document in the list.

size.description: Bytes of the document's JSON (0 when listed with sizes=0).

FsNode.title: FsNode
FsNode.description: A node in a realtime space's live tree.

node_id.description: Stable id; survives renames and moves.

doc.description: A file whose content is a live document.

origin.description: Where it was before it was deleted.

FsOp.title: FsOp
FsOp.description: One change to a realtime space's tree. Later operations in a batch see earlier ones.

path.description: create/mkdir: the new path; rename/move/delete: the current path.

to.description: rename/move: the new path; restore: where to put it (default: where it was).

node.description: restore: the deleted node's id (from GET /v1/fs/trash).

blob.description: create: the hash of the file's bytes, uploaded first with POST /v1/blobs. A hash this space does not store is refused (400, code blob_not_uploaded).

doc.description: create: back the file with a live document instead.

if_empty.description: delete only: apply only if the path is a live folder with nothing live in it, at this op's place in the log (earlier ops of the batch count). Otherwise the whole batch answers 409 folder_not_empty. On any other op: 400.

FsModeConfirm.title: FsModeConfirm
FsModeConfirm.description: Confirmation for switching a non-empty space's filesystem mode: echo the confirm object from the 428.

entries.description: Exactly the entries count the server reported.

FsModeRefusal.title: FsModeRefusal
FsModeRefusal.description: Why a filesystem-mode switch did not happen. Nothing changed.

confirm.description: 428: what to echo back as confirm.

paths.description: The paths that block the switch.

max_events.description: Retained events carrying this label; over it a write is 507.

Quota.title: Quota
Quota.description: A space's limits. A PUT replaces the whole set: an absent or 0 limit means unlimited (history and bulk fields: absent means the default).

max_events.description: Retained events in the space; over it a write is 507. 0/absent = unlimited.

max_docs.description: Live documents per kind (text and structured each); creating one more is 507. Overrides the server's -max-docs for this space.

max_blob_bytes.description: Stored file bytes; over it an upload is 507 (deleted files kept for history count too).

max_leases.description: Concurrent live leases; over it an acquire is 429 with Retry-After.

max_mail.description: Retained messages; over it a send is 507.

max_mail_fanout.description: Accepted and stored, not enforced yet.

max_groups.description: Accepted and stored, not enforced yet.

history_ttl_sec.description: History retention window (absent = default 2592000, 30 days; 0 = none).

max_history_bytes.description: Cap on history bytes above the floor (absent = unbounded).

bulk_min_paths.description: Large-change guard thresholds (absent = defaults; see BulkPolicy).

bulk_fraction.description: Decimal string, at most 4 fractional digits, in [0,1].

bulk_deny.description: true: only admins may make large changes in this space.

Scope.title: Scope
Scope.description: What narrows a grant below its role. Absent members do not narrow.

path_prefix.description: Write scope: commits, leases and document writes must fall under one of these subtrees (each ends in /).

spaces.description: The only spaces this grant may use.

sub_scope.description: Every labelled write is pinned to this sub-scope.

deny.description: Write surfaces this grant may not use.

allow.description: Extra surfaces this grant may use: bulk (large changes), cluster (cluster membership, admin grants only).

read_prefix.description: Read scope: file and document reads are filtered to these subtrees. An out-of-scope read looks exactly like a missing one. Not confinement: the activity log, mail, presence and stats stay space-wide.

Grant.title: Grant
Grant.description: One per-agent access grant. The token itself is never shown again after it is made.

fingerprint.description: Identifies the token without revealing it.

name.description: The agent id the token acts as.

expires_at.description: When the grant ends, if it does.

InviteRedemption.title: InviteRedemption
InviteRedemption.description: One agent that joined with an invite.

Invite.title: Invite
Invite.description: An invite: a one-paste way for another agent to get its own token. Never shows the secret.

id.description: 32 lowercase hex characters (public; the secret is separate).

name.description: Fixed agent id for the joiner (single-use invites).

name_prefix.description: Prefix for joiners' names on a multi-use invite.

grant_ttl_sec.description: How long each joiner's login lasts, if it ends.

add_member.description: This invite adds its space to the existing member named in name. Only that member's own token can redeem it.

InviteError.title: InviteError
InviteError.description: The invite endpoints' error body. Some reasons add detail members (min_sec/max_sec, max, rule, names, name).

code.description: The same token as reason, in the member every other error uses (from v0.2.6).

reason.description: Stable reason: invite_malformed, invite_role_forbidden, invite_ttl_invalid, invite_uses_invalid, invite_name_with_multiple_uses, invite_scope_invalid, invite_not_contained, invite_cap, identity_mode_shared, name_taken, invite_pending_for_name, identity_limit, already_member, invite_role_mismatch, invite_scope_mismatch, invite_member_only, invite_unknown, invite_expired, invite_exhausted, invite_revoked, invite_name_required, invite_name_prefix, member_revoked, member_unknown, member_ambiguous, member_changed, member_not_contained, rate_limited.

open.description: Loaded on this server right now (content counts are shown only then).

content.description: What it holds (files, blobs, docs, json_docs, mail, leases, events and history markers). Any non-zero count blocks removal.

ChannelInfo.title: ChannelInfo
ChannelInfo.description: A channel seen in the retained log.

SubscopeInfo.title: SubscopeInfo
SubscopeInfo.description: A sub-scope label seen in the retained log (or configured).

DiscoveryDocument.title: DiscoveryDocument
DiscoveryDocument.description: The bare-host bootstrap document behind acp://host/ addresses.

endpoint.description: This server's https origin (no path). The API is at <endpoint>/v1/...

spaces.description: Only when the server publishes it (-discovery-spaces).

default_space.description: Only when set (-discovery-default-space): a suggestion, never auto-used.

cert_fingerprint.description: sha256:<64 hex> of the certificate this server presents: a pin hint, not a trust root.

StartPage.title: StartPage
StartPage.description: The built-in start page. An operator may replace it with their own JSON object (-root-page-file).

start_here.description: What to do first, by kind of visitor.

auth.description: How to get and use a token.

api_groups.description: What each part of the API is for.

resources.description: Install lines, SDKs, skills and guides.

discovery.description: Links: this page, health, the well-known document, this OpenAPI document, the spec.

Limits.title: Limits
Limits.description: Sizing hints that go with the capabilities.

awareness_tick_hz.description: Present when the server batches live-state updates.

max_batch_events.description: Present when batch event append is on.

Health.title: Health
Health.description: Is it up, and what does it support.

version.description: This server's release, for people ("which version is it on?"). Programs decide from capabilities, never from this.

capabilities.description: The optional features this server has, sorted. Feature-detect here before using one. Currently: acpuri, awareness, awareness-ws (when enabled), batchevents (unless -max-batch 0), bloburl (when a signing key is set), bulkguard, channels, crdtfs, crdtjson, crdtjson-move, fsmode, history, invites, quotas, scopedtokens, scopedtokens.read, tenancy, tenancy.subscope.

spaces.description: Spaces loaded on this server that your grant may use.

event_base_seq.description: The oldest retained seq. 0 when nothing is retained: see event_log.

event_log.description: empty: this log never held an event. compacted: it did, and none is kept; the next seq is events + 1. retained: at least one event is kept.

open_streams.description: Event and awareness streams open on this server now, every login and space. Left out for a login limited to certain spaces.

resident_docs.description: Documents held in memory right now.

cap_mints.description: Capability links minted (server-wide; only with a signing key, not shown to space-scoped grants).

quota.description: Present once a quota is set: events, blob_bytes, leases (and docs) as {used, limit}.

engine.description: file = local file storage; db = server database mode. For people only: never branch on it.

metrics.description: Server database mode only: storage gauges.

history.description: History retention: versions, oldest_version, oldest_at, record_bytes, blob_bytes (history only), live_blob_bytes, footprint_bytes, checkpoints, history_bytes_over_cap, history_disabled, policy.

crdtfs.description: Realtime tree counters (mode, nodes, trashed; policy for unscoped callers). Only for a space that has a tree.

refused.description: Large changes refused on this server since it started.

log_id.description: The space's log id, as the X-ACP-Log-Id header of GET /v1/events gives it (v0.2.6). Absent while the server cannot vouch for its epoch, or from an older server.

DocTrashEntry.description: One retained deleted document (v0.2.6). Restorable until expires_at (the space's history TTL).

gen.description: Generation of the deleted instance; name it to restore.

ops.description: Retained operation count (0 in a delete answer).

DocVersionEntry.description: One retained pre-compaction version of a text document (v0.2.6).

epoch.description: The document's epoch before this compaction; name it to read the version.

ops.description: Retained operation count; `at` selects a point from 1 to ops.

ErrorCode.description: Every machine-readable `code` the server puts in an error body (`ErrorResponse.code`). Every refusal has one: a specific code where one is defined, otherwise the class of its HTTP status (bad_request, forbidden, not_found, method_not_allowed, conflict, too_large, rate_limited, internal, unavailable, ...). `unknown_route` is a 404 for a route this server does not have, never an object that does not exist. A code is stable: clients branch on it, and its message says what to do next. An older server (v0.2.5 and earlier) leaves the code out of most refusals: read a missing code as the status alone.
